request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Use fold-level evidence to decide: a config that wins a majority of folds is more trustworthy than one with a higher mean but inconsistent fold performance. Between two configs with similar fold-win rates, prefer the simpler model. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means one config clearly wins most folds and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means fold wins are split roughly evenly or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run. Compare fold-by-fold: count how many folds each config wins to assess which is genuinely better vs lucky. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Run 1 wins all 5 folds against both run 2 and run 3 (0.7831 vs 0.7669 vs 0.7396, 0.7304 vs 0.7053 vs 0.6692, 0.6273 vs 0.6142 vs 0.5712, 0.8014 vs 0.7947 vs 0.7676, 0.7312 vs 0.6901 vs 0.6878), so the ranking is consistent, but only 3 configs have been tried.

Fold-to-fold SD of about 0.07 is large relative to the 0.02 gap between run 1 and run 3, so the margin over run 3 is modest even though the fold ordering is consistent. Fold 3 is weak for every config (0.57-0.63), which suggests a harder provider subset or a temporal/distribution shift.

The PotentialFraud label has an undocumented origin and may be a rule-based or investigator-derived flag. A ROC-AUC of 0.94 and PR-AUC of 0.73 with a 9% base rate is strong and may reflect label leakage or proxy features, such as claim-volume or size features that encode the labeling process, rather than genuine fraud signal. Treat the model output as a suspicion ranking only.

The 'all' feature set includes size/volume features, which may act as proxies for the label. Run 1 beats no_size configs, but those also changed model and imbalance, so the size effect is confounded with other changes.
Claims span only about 13 months, and it is unclear whether CV was grouped or time-aware. Provider-level leakage across folds is possible if the splits are not stratified or grouped properly.

Precision@50 is 0.76 for run 1 and 0.77 for run 3, which is essentially tied. The audit queue holds about 100 providers, so precision@100 was not reported and would be more relevant. Run 1 has no class weighting and is also the more complex feature set, but it still wins on PR-AUC across every fold.

next_experiments.rationale: Isolates the effect of size features by holding run 1's hyperparameters and imbalance setting fixed and removing only size features. This tests whether run 1's lead comes from size proxies or label-process leakage.
Simple baseline to check whether the gain from boosting is real. If a linear model comes close, it would be preferable on simplicity and would hint at an easy proxy signal.
Tests a smaller, more regularized LightGBM on the full feature set to see whether run 1's complexity is needed, given the high fold variance.
